subject: Greenline: EU-only inference + forced-model variant (no fallback)
messages:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Customer ask: Greenline requires EU-only routing + model variant

Kim — quick handoff from the Greenline AE. Customer (Greenline Health) has an explicit regulatory requirement to keep inference in EU regions and for us to serve them with only the validated quantized variant they certified: "redwood-quant-eu-1". They are asking for two hard constraints: (1) no cross-region fallback (requests must never be routed outside EU), and (2) forced model selection (no automatic fallback to fallback-compatible models or higher-latency variants).

They attached the model validation spreadsheet and a short SOC2 excerpt where the requirement is called out. AE says this is a gating item for procurement. Can you advise whether product can bless a customer-scoped routing/fallback exception, what the risk/cost delta looks like, and if there are any telemetry or audit changes we should push to meet their compliance ask?

Attachments: greenline-model-preference.xlsx, greenline-soc2-excerpt.pdf

— Priyom
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — forwarding to infra & product leads for feasibility. Quick asks from product side:
- Is the requirement global for the entire account or scoped to specific routes / API keys? (this affects routing policy granularity)
- Do they require absolute hard enforcement (i.e., service-level guarantee + contract language) or would an operational control (we turn off cross-region failover for their account) suffice?

Karthik — can you outline the operational implications of a per-account region hardlock and forced model pin? In particular: impact on failover, autoscaling, warm cache (KV) behavior, and SLO risks. Also note any additional billing / dedicated capacity recommendations.

Marissa / Lauren — heads-up: this likely touches procurement terms (region guarantees) and may need tighter breach clauses. Please flag anything I should loop legal on.

If it's helpful, I can schedule a 30-min sync with Greenline + infra.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer ask: Greenline requires EU-only routing + model variant

Short answer: technically possible but non-trivial. Notes:
- Per-account region hardlock: we can add an account-level routing policy that pins region to eu-west-1/eu-west-2. This disables automatic region-level failover for that account.
- Forced model selection (pin to redwood-quant-eu-1): we can enforce a per-account model allowlist. However, if that model becomes unavailable (OOM, upgrade), we currently have no automated safe fallback — requests would queue or fail unless owner opts into a compatible fallback.
- Operational costs: without fallback you'll see increased error spikes during model OOMs or maintenance windows. Warm-up for a quantized model in dedicated pools is slower; cold-cache latency will increase for initial bursts (KV cache miss impacts).
- Autoscaling: to keep SLOs we'll likely need a dedicated or reserve capacity commitment for predictable throughput — otherwise customers will see throttles.
- Telemetry: we should add an account-scoped audit flag: any request denied due to fallback policy should be logged, with token-level cost and region tags.

Recommendation: two paths — (A) Offer Dedicated-Reserved EU capacity + forced model pin (SLA & stable environment) or (B) Hosted with an operational agreement: disable automatic fallback but include a manual emergency fallback policy (requires 15–30 min to enable). Path A is safer for both parties.

I'll draft a short tech note and cost delta estimate if product/legal want to present it.

— Karthik
Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-13T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer ask: Greenline requires EU-only routing + model variant

Legal/procurement notes:
- If Greenline insists on contract language promising "no cross-border processing under any circumstance" we need to run this by InfoSec and the contracts team. Absolute guarantees are risky without Dedicated or Private deployment.
- We should avoid broad SLA promises about model availability when a customer requires a single pinned model. Consider a negotiated uptime SLA tied to Dedicated capacity, with an approved emergency playbook (manual fallback) described in the contract.
- Please route their SOC / certification docs to our compliance bucket (I cc'd Marissa). Greenline's SOC2 excerpt looks straightforward but we'll need the full report if procurement proceeds.

Next steps from legal: get the full SOC2 + attestation, and decision on whether they'll accept a Dedicated reservation. If they want hosted + hardlock, we need explicit written acceptance of potential outages during model unavailability windows.

— Lauren
Senior Director, Revenue Ops & Legal
Redwood Inference
